scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false) not the author's working copy. Python FastAPI backend and Vue 3 frontend; routes were taken from backend/garminview/api/main.py and the routers; no authentication or authorization dependency exists anywhere in the API (only the get_db dependency), so every route is auth_detected false. Route severity follows the calibration pattern: sensitivity of data and write capability, with the compensating factor that the Docker backend itself publishes no host port (only the Caddy frontend on 8080 is published, and its proxy regex forwards health, training, body, admin, sync, activities, assessments, export, nutrition paths to the backend; /actalog read paths are not proxied by Caddy but /admin/actalog is). Because the API binds 0.0.0.0 inside the container and defaults to the author's LAN, who can reach it depends on deployment. backend/.env was not read in full: only variable names and 4-character prefixes were examined and redacted. Also tracked in git: backend/garmindb.log, backend/logs/sync.log, backend/logs/uvicorn.log and docs/myfitnesspal/File-Export-2012-03-24-to-2026-03-11.zip (personal MyFitnessPal export, not opened). Excluded as test fixtures/false positives: raw 'weight' sensitive-data hits (exercise weight), test.example hosts, tests/. Shell scripts (entrypoint.sh, prep.sh) and GitHub Actions YAML are out of scope for deep detection in v1.0. Marimo notebooks under backend/notebooks are Python and were treated as such.

sql_injection_risk.reason: backend/garminview/api/routes/admin.py:76 builds 'ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN {col} {definition}' with an f-string, but both values come from a hardcoded list; scripts/migrate_to_mariadb.py:91 interpolates table names from inspected schema. No user-controlled input reaches either. All other queries use SQLAlchemy ORM or bound parameters (latent risk only).

what_this_app_can_do: Shows personal Garmin (and Polar/MyFitnessPal/Actalog) health and training data - sleep, HR, weight, activities, training load, nutrition - in a web dashboard, to anyone who can reach the server; no login is required.
Lets anyone who can reach it export health metrics as CSV or JSON for any date range.

Lets anyone who can reach it read all app configuration (including the stored Actalog password), change configuration and schedules, upload MyFitnessPal exports, trigger Garmin downloads and Actalog syncs, and import files from a server directory path.
Runs scheduled background syncs against Garmin Connect via GarminDB and against an Actalog server, and parses workout notes with a configurable LLM endpoint.

Ollama / OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (workout note text)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Whoever can reach the published frontend port (default 8080 on the host, listening on all interfaces) - the API behind it has no authentication on any route. In local development it is reachable from the same machine only if bound to localhost.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: backend/.env is tracked in git and contains a database connection string with credentials (value redacted)
GET /admin/config returns all app_config values, including the stored Actalog password in plaintext, without any authentication
/export/csv and /export/json return bulk personal health data without authentication
POST /admin/actalog/test-connection makes outbound requests to a caller-supplied URL (SSRF-style) without authentication
Workout note text is sent to a configurable LLM endpoint; if that is a third-party service, user data leaves the network
A personal MyFitnessPal export zip and sync logs are committed to the repository

top_findings: No authentication on any API route, including admin, config, export and sync endpoints
backend/.env with a credential-bearing database URL is tracked in git (critical)
GET /admin/config exposes the stored Actalog password; /export/* returns bulk personal health data (critical)
